title: FAA Part 107 Loading and performance practice questions
description: Free Part 107 practice questions on loading and performance: CG and lift, stability, load factor, overloading and performance data, with FAA sources.

questions.question: According to the FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide, whose weight and balance restrictions for an aircraft should be closely followed?

options.A: The local air traffic control facility's
options.B: Those established by the manufacturer or the builder
options.C: The visual observer's
options.D: Those of the nearest airport operator

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "An aircraft's weight and balance restrictions established by the manufacturer or the builder should be closely followed."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: A manufacturer lists a maximum gross takeoff weight for a small UA. What does the Study Guide say about taking off with that load?

options.A: It is safe under all conditions because the manufacturer specified it
options.B: It applies only to fixed-wing aircraft
options.C: It may be exceeded at high elevations
options.D: The aircraft may not always safely take off with this load under all conditions

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "Although a maximum gross takeoff weight may be specified, the aircraft may not always safely take off with this load under all conditions."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what is the most common weight change that takes place during flight?

options.A: Fuel burn
options.B: Rain collecting on the airframe
options.C: Battery drain at the control station
options.D: Ice forming on the propellers

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "Fuel burn is the most common weight change that takes place during flight."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: A small UA weighs 49 pounds with its battery, and the operator attaches a 7-pound camera before takeoff. Under the 107.3 definition, is it a small unmanned aircraft?

options.A: Yes, because a camera payload is not counted
options.B: Yes, because only the empty weight counts
options.C: No, because its takeoff weight with everything on board or attached is 56 pounds, which is not less than 55 pounds
options.D: Yes, because the weight limit applies only after takeoff

questions.explanation: 107.3: "Small unmanned aircraft means an unmanned aircraft weighing less than 55 pounds on takeoff, including everything that is on board or otherwise attached to the aircraft." Here 49 + 7 = 56 pounds.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.3, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what would happen if an aircraft were supported at its exact center of gravity (CG)?

options.A: It would balance in any attitude
options.B: It would pitch nose down
options.C: It would pitch nose up
options.D: It would roll toward the heavier wing

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "If the aircraft were supported at its exact CG, it would balance in any attitude."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: An aircraft's CG is forward of its center of pressure (CP). According to the Study Guide, what tendency does this create?

options.A: A nose-up pitching moment
options.B: A tendency to roll left
options.C: A natural tendency to pitch nose down
options.D: No pitching tendency at all

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "When the CG is forward of the CP, there is a natural tendency for the aircraft to want to pitch nose down."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, where do designers fix the aft limit of the CG in order to retain flight equilibrium?

options.A: Aft of the CP
options.B: Forward of the CP for the corresponding flight speed
options.C: Exactly at the CP at all flight speeds
options.D: At the aircraft's geometric center

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "designers fix the aft limit of the CG forward of the CP for the corresponding flight speed in order to retain flight equilibrium."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: A small UA in stabilized level flight starts producing less lift than its weight. What does the Study Guide say happens to the vertical speed?

options.A: It will increase
options.B: It stays the same because the aircraft remains in equilibrium
options.C: It increases until the aircraft accelerates upward
options.D: It will decrease

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "If lift becomes less than weight, the vertical speed will decrease." Only when lift equals weight is the aircraft "in a state of equilibrium".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: How does the Study Guide characterize stability?

options.A: Primarily a matter of piloting technique
options.B: Primarily an aircraft design characteristic
options.C: A quality set by the weather on the day of flight
options.D: A quality the remote pilot sets in the control station software

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says stability "is primarily an aircraft design characteristic."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Which description does the Study Guide give for controllability?

options.A: The capability of an aircraft to respond to the pilot's control, especially with regard to flight path and attitude
options.B: The inherent quality of an aircraft to return to its original flight path after a disturbance
options.C: The quality that lets an aircraft withstand the stresses imposed by maneuvers
options.D: The ability of an aircraft to carry its maximum payload

questions.explanation: The Study Guide defines controllability as "the capability of an aircraft to respond to the pilot's control, especially with regard to flight path and attitude."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Which factors does the Study Guide say govern an aircraft's maneuverability?

options.A: Ambient temperature, humidity and pressure
options.B: The pilot's experience and training only
options.C: Weight, inertia, size and location of flight controls, structural strength, and powerplant
options.D: The control link frequency and range

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says maneuverability "is governed by the aircraft's weight, inertia, size and location of flight controls, structural strength, and powerplant."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: For any given bank angle, how does the Study Guide say the rate of turn varies with airspeed?

options.A: The higher the speed, the faster the rate of turn
options.B: The rate of turn does not depend on airspeed
options.C: The rate of turn depends only on aircraft weight
options.D: The higher the speed, the slower the rate of turn

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "For any given bank angle, the rate-of-turn varies with the airspeed—the higher the speed, the slower the rate-of-turn (ROT)."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: An aircraft with a normal unaccelerated stalling speed of 45 knots is banked greater than 72° in a steep turn. Which airspeed does the Study Guide say it must be kept greater than to prevent inducing a stall?

options.A: 75 knots
options.B: 45 knots
options.C: 54 knots
options.D: 60 knots

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says banking greater than 72° "produces a load factor of 3" and that with a 45-knot stalling speed "the airspeed must be kept greater than 75 knots to prevent inducing a stall."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, in which maneuvers should a pilot be aware of the danger of inadvertently stalling the aircraft by increasing the load factor?

options.A: Straight-and-level flight at a constant airspeed
options.B: A shallow, straight descent at a constant airspeed
options.C: Holding a steady heading at cruise speed
options.D: A steep turn or spiral

questions.explanation: "A pilot should be aware of the danger of inadvertently stalling the aircraft by increasing the load factor, as in a steep turn or spiral."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: A remote pilot attaches a payload that leaves the CG outside the approved limits. What does the Study Guide say operating this way results in?

options.A: Improved maneuverability
options.B: A lower stalling speed
options.C: Control difficulty
options.D: Longer range

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "Operation with the center of gravity (CG) outside the approved limits results in control difficulty."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Which factors does the Study Guide name as limiting the amount of lift an airfoil produces?

options.A: Only the aircraft's weight
options.B: The airfoil design, angle of attack, airspeed, and air density
options.C: Only the battery's state of charge
options.D: The distance between the aircraft and the control station

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "The amount of lift produced by an airfoil is limited by the airfoil design, AOA, airspeed, and air density."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: A remote pilot did not load the aircraft properly. According to the Study Guide, when does the initial indication of poor performance usually take place?

options.A: During landing
options.B: Only after the battery is half drained
options.C: During cruise at maximum altitude
options.D: During takeoff

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "If not properly loaded, the initial indication of poor performance usually takes place during takeoff." An overloaded aircraft "may not be able to leave the ground".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what must an aircraft do to maintain a given altitude and speed when weight is added to it?

options.A: Fly at a higher angle of attack, which increases induced and parasite drag
options.B: Fly at a lower angle of attack, which reduces drag
options.C: Keep the same angle of attack and gain reserve thrust
options.D: Fly at a lower angle of attack, which reduces parasite drag only

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "If weight is added to an aircraft, it must fly at a higher angle of attack (AOA) to maintain a given altitude and speed." This "increases the induced drag of the wings, as well as the parasite drag of the aircraft."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Why does the Study Guide say the climb performance of an aircraft diminishes with altitude?

options.A: An increase in altitude decreases the power required and increases the power available
options.B: Air density increases with altitude
options.C: An increase in altitude increases the power required and decreases the power available
options.D: The aircraft's weight increases with altitude

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "An increase in altitude also increases the power required and decreases the power available. Therefore, the climb performance of an aircraft diminishes with altitude."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Which operational performance data does the Study Guide say a manufacturer may provide for an aircraft?

options.A: Airspace class boundaries and NOTAM codes
options.B: Data pertaining to takeoff, climb, range, endurance, descent, and landing
options.C: Remote pilot medical and certificate records
options.D: METAR and TAF codes for the launch site

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says the manufacturer may provide "operational performance data for the aircraft such as data pertaining to takeoff, climb, range, endurance, descent, and landing."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)
